problem: Portal V2 v1 established a single responsive experience authority, but release assurance still covered only a smaller visual matrix and did not make dynamic visual overflow/runtime experience failures first-class release signals.
rootCause: The baseline experience contract and visual assurance existed as separate strengths. Without consolidating 320px coverage, dynamic visual remeasurement, touch-target enforcement and runtime signals into the same authority, future page modules could regress after mount or at narrow widths without a deterministic fail-closed release signal.

preventionRule: Keep portal-v2/experience.css and portal-v2/experience.js as the sole UX authority; dynamically normalize and remeasure visuals; fail assurance on >2px page or visual overflow, missing experience runtime or critical controls below 44px; test six critical routes at 1440, 1024, 390 and 320px; preserve canonical Portal State fail-closed backend authority.
prevention: One canonical portal experience CSS/JS authority; parallel product-experience stacks are forbidden.
Six critical routes times four viewports must yield 24 screenshot/metric cases.
320px narrow-mobile and 390px mobile are first-class release surfaces.
Dynamic visuals are normalized after mount and remeasured with ResizeObserver.
Visual overflow, runtime errors and route interactions emit Powerhouse experience signals.
Critical navigation and action controls remain at least 44px.
Portal State authentication and stored=false behavior remain fail-closed and unchanged.
